name: Rismorelin

lead: Rismorelin is a growth hormone-releasing hormone (GHRH) analog, a peptide that signals the pituitary to release growth hormone.
People interested in physique follow this class because growth hormone is associated with lean mass and recovery. Rismorelin itself is much less documented than relatives such as sermorelin.

paras: It is classed as a GHRH receptor agonist: it binds the GHRH receptor on the pituitary and prompts growth hormone release, which for related compounds occurs in pulses limited by somatostatin feedback.
Little specific safety information is published for rismorelin. It is not a marketed approved product, and related GHRH peptides are available mainly through prescription or compounding channels.

angle.text: People who use GHRH analogs aim to raise growth hormone release to support leaner body composition and recovery from training. Rismorelin belongs to this group, though it is discussed far less than its relatives.

lead: Rismorelin is a synthetic peptide in the growth hormone-releasing hormone (GHRH) analog family, the group of compounds that prompt the pituitary gland to release the body's own growth hormone. People interested in physique and recovery follow this family because growth hormone signalling is associated with lean mass, fat distribution and tissue repair, which feed into how a physique looks.[1]

Rismorelin is listed alongside sermorelin, the better-known 29-amino-acid GHRH fragment, as a GHRH receptor agonist.[1] Published human data on rismorelin itself are scarce, and its public footprint is much smaller than that of sermorelin or tesamorelin.
infobox: Not marketed as an approved product

paras: GHRH analogs bind the GHRH receptor on pituitary somatotroph cells and stimulate release of growth hormone. For the related compound sermorelin, the resulting release occurs in bursts rather than as a constant level, because somatostatin feedback limits the response.[1]

Rismorelin is named in lists of GHRH receptor agonists, but it does not have a dedicated encyclopedia article, and it is far less discussed in training and looksmaxxing communities than sermorelin, which was sold as Geref until its manufacturer stopped production in 2008.[1] Sermorelin remains obtainable through compounding pharmacies according to the same source.[1]
